why: Must_not 1 holds. Check 3 fails whenever any export has no heading ("for example slugify or padLeft"), so a README with a padLeft section but no slugify section cannot pass. Checks 1 and 2 do not demand a one-character fill or a parameter count, and the multi-character fill case is only advisory. Must_not 2 breaks, though. Check 3's command is wrapped in bash double quotes, so `'\\b'` reaches JS as `'\b'`, which is a backspace character, not a word boundary. No heading can match, so every function is reported missing and even a correct README fails. That FAIL condition is stricter than line 3. Check 4 also requires the output to show `# fail 0`, which only appears in TAP reporter output. Node's spec reporter prints `ℹ fail 0` instead, so a passing `npm test` with exit 0 could still fail. That is stricter than "npm test passes".
